_comment: Routing policy: what the controller is allowed to choose automatically, and why. This file is data on purpose — tiers, cost weights, quality floors and ceilings belong to the operator, not to code. The installer treats it as CONFIRM: a shipped change is shown as a diff and applied only with your say-so, so local cost and entitlement customisations are never overwritten silently.
_costUnits: costWeight and effortCostMultiplier are RELATIVE weights, not money. There are no provider prices in this file and none may be added as bare numbers: if monetary pricing is ever configured it must carry a source, a currency and an effectiveAt date, and estimates stay labelled estimates until it does.
_specialistCaps: maxSpecialistsPerStage is the fan-out allowed on ONE stage: one method for standard work, two complementary ones for complex work, three (including an independent reviewer) for critical work. maxSpecialists bounds the whole run so a wide plan cannot accumulate an unbounded agent count.
_expectedRetry: Probability that an attempt at this tier, for this band, has to be repeated. This is what stops 'minimise cost' from meaning 'always pick the cheapest model': expected cost is costUnits x (1 + p), so an underpowered attempt on complex work is correctly scored as the expensive option.
_providers: Policy metadata for the catalogue the router may select from. Before automatic planning, current Codex and Gemini availability is refreshed from their installed clients and intersected with these entries; newly discovered models receive deterministic fallback classification. Claude aliases track the latest family offered by Claude Code. The console consumes the same cached availability. The ambiguous 'default' model and 'ultra' effort remain outside automatic routing.

anthropic.label: Claude (Anthropic account)
anthropic._evidence: Workload profiles and relative weights refreshed 2026-09-29 from https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5 and https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5. Family aliases are retained because Claude Code resolves them to the current available family model.

models.label: Claude Haiku (latest alias)
limitations: not for ambiguous synthesis, architecture or security judgement

models.label: Claude Sonnet (latest alias)
limitations: thin on novel architecture and adversarial reconciliation

models.label: Claude Opus (latest alias)
limitations: xhigh is Opus-specific; it is not a routine default

bedrock.label: Claude Code on Bedrock
bedrock._evidence: Uses the same current Claude family workload profiles as Anthropic routing; availability remains governed by the configured Bedrock account and region.

models.label: Claude Haiku (latest Bedrock alias)
limitations: no native WebSearch on Bedrock; use the run-scoped isolated browser for external evidence

models.label: Claude Sonnet (latest Bedrock alias)
limitations: no native WebSearch on Bedrock; use the run-scoped isolated browser or pair with a second researcher

models.label: Claude Opus (latest Bedrock alias)
limitations: no native WebSearch on Bedrock; run-scoped isolated browser available

codex.label: ChatGPT / Codex
codex._note: A different provider family, not a rank-for-rank equivalent of the Claude tiers. Tiers here say what this policy is willing to spend on which class of work; they do not assert parity between vendors.
codex._evidence: Workload profiles and relative weights refreshed 2026-09-29 from https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model?model=gpt-6-astra and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing. Live Codex discovery remains the availability boundary.

models.label: GPT-6 Luna
limitations: best for focused, repeatable and high-volume work; not the default for difficult architecture or security judgement

gemini.label: Gemini through Antigravity
gemini._note: Availability and exact effort-bearing model IDs are refreshed from `agy models` before automatic routing. These entries are the offline fallback and the policy metadata for known models.

_unroutable: Identities whose surface exposes no model or effort choice. They remain fully assignable to roles; the router simply reports that it has nothing to select for them rather than inventing a combination.

unroutableKinds.copilot-studio: a chat endpoint over the Microsoft estate; model and effort are the tenant's, not this controller's

_floors: A quality floor is the lowest tier and effort an automatic route may use. It is a floor, never a target: a higher choice is always permitted, a lower one never is.
_escalation: The only ladder an automatic escalation may climb, in order. A rung above the band's maxAutomaticTier/maxAutomaticEffort is unreachable without an explicit operator approval, and no rung exists above the last one here.
_specialists: role -> the focused method (a toolkit sub-agent definition) that role uses. A null method means the work is done by the account holding the role directly; the controller does not invent a specialist to have one.
_independentReview: The method used when a critical run needs a check whose value is that it did not come from the producer. It is only called independent when a DIFFERENT eligible identity holds it; otherwise the route says so and the existing degraded-operation approval applies.
